summary: Identity-first design. No account/connection-string keys on the data plane; managed identity + data-plane RBAC for every hop. All gates pass.

checks.evidence: infra/modules/rbac.bicep assigns Cosmos SQL data-plane role (00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002), Search Index Data Reader/Contributor, Storage Blob Data Reader/Contributor, Cognitive Services OpenAI User, and Azure Service Bus Data Sender/Receiver to the api/worker/scheduler/search identities.
role_assignments: Cosmos DB Built-in Data Contributor -> casewright-api, casewright-worker
Storage Blob Data Contributor -> casewright-worker, search-service
Cognitive Services OpenAI User -> casewright-api, search-service
Azure Service Bus Data Sender -> casewright-api, casewright-scheduler
Azure Service Bus Data Receiver -> casewright-worker

checks.evidence: storage.bicep allowSharedKeyAccess=false; search.bicep disableLocalAuth=true authOptions absent; servicebus.bicep disableLocalAuth=true; cosmos.bicep disableKeyBasedMetadataWriteAccess=true and data-plane SQL role used instead of keys; openai.bicep disableLocalAuth=true (Entra-only).

Search-to-OpenAI vectorizer and embedding skill authenticate via the Search service system-assigned identity (Cognitive Services OpenAI User). Search-to-Storage data source uses ResourceId= managed identity, not AccountKey=. No apiKey present in skillset/datasource definitions.

Container Apps + Function App use user-assigned managed identity; Search uses system-assigned identity. No secrets in app settings except optional Graph app secret stored in Key Vault and referenced via Key Vault reference.

findings.message: Microsoft Graph (SharePoint) app-only auth may require a client secret if certificate auth is not provisioned; stored in Key Vault and surfaced via Key Vault reference, never inlined.
